title: What Does a Software Engineer Look Like? Exploring Societal Stereotypes in LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the selection frequency of male versus female candidates in AI-generated text hiring recommendations (using both gendered and gender-neutral prompts), and visually coding the perceived gender of individuals in AI-generated images across different software engineering seniority levels.

Analyzing textual candidate selections for racial representation, and visually coding AI-generated images for perceived race/ethnicity and skin tone lightness/darkness using the Massey Martin NIS skin tone scale.
Categorizing the apparent age group (e.g., under 30, mid-20s, older) of individuals depicted in AI-generated images for various junior and senior software engineering roles.
Evaluating the geographical locations of recommended candidates in text outputs to detect AI preferences for candidates from the Global North (e.g., Western countries) versus the Global South.
Coding AI-generated images using a body silhouette scale to assess the diversity of body sizes and shapes represented in the depictions of software engineers.
Analyzing AI-generated candidate images for the presence and distribution of cultural attire (Western vs. non-Western) and specific religious symbols (e.g., hijabs, kippahs, crosses).
Examining AI-generated images for the presence, absence, or representation of visible disabilities (such as mobility aids, vision aids, or prosthetics).
